chapters.title: Why use MOMM?
chapters.text: One agent writes. Others challenge it. You keep the evidence. Mom gives your coding agent independent review claims from the provider tools you already use. The benefit is a checkable decision trail, not a guarantee that a group of models is right. This tour shows the actual interfaces, with screen actions accelerated fifteen times and narration at normal speed.

chapters.title: Install or upgrade deliberately
chapters.text: New user? Open Get started. Keep the skills clone in a permanent folder, choose your harness, and inspect the installation preview before applying it. Existing user? Copy the upgrade prompt. Your agent checks the newest stable release and preserves your login sessions, other skills, and private ledgers. Older installations may need the verified bootstrap described in the guide. Never confuse a draft branch with a release. Review every protocol change before accepting it.

chapters.title: Your Setup Center
chapters.text: The Setup Center is for connecting and maintaining reviewer tools. See the installed versions, choose your governor, and check the routes you intend to use. Latest version checks and updates are separate actions. Installing a tool does not prove its account can review. Quotas, network access and login storage can still block it. Browser login stays yours to complete. No secret keys are needed.

chapters.title: Finish the review loop
chapters.text: Run the review from your project, using the installed skill path. Approve the providers before sharing code. The governor does not review itself. Peer findings are claims. Your agent investigates material findings, writes any supported fix, runs tests, and records a decision for every suggestion. Deferred means still open. A completed review needs the governor's evidence checks, not just positive votes or a matching decision count.

chapters.title: Open the evidence ledger
chapters.text: The ledger answers who said what and what happened next. This public example is a sanitized historical snapshot, not your private dashboard. It contains a hundred and fifty three runs, a hundred and thirty nine stored reports, and five hundred and seventy decisions. Charts show timing, verdicts and failures with their denominators. Applied decisions are the developer's judgments, not independently measured accuracy. Current release checks are shown separately.

chapters.title: Start small. Keep the proof.
chapters.text: Mom also reviews prose, and selected routes support images or other attachments. Capability depends on the actual tool, not the logo. Start with a small approved project and one available external reviewer. Keep your tests, close the decisions, and save the ledger somewhere permanent. Use the current release link on the page for later updates. Nothing installs or updates automatically.
